properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean strata comprise Carboniferous sedimentary sandstones and siltstones of the Gullane Formation, underlain by glacial till and volcanic quartz-dolerite intrusions (Castle Rock crag). Primary masonry lithology consists of local pale-buff Craigleith and Hailes sandstone (calciferous quartz-arenite), bound with historic hydraulic lime mortar.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Queen Street Gardens woodland flank containing mature *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm), *Fagus sylvatica* (Common Beech), and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Late December phenology: complete winter defoliation, bare dark timber canopies, intricate branch silhouettes, and dormant understory turf.

properties.architectural_summary: Linear Georgian classical terrace row along Queen Street (James Craig New Town plan). Structures feature 3- to 4-storey residential blocks over sunken basement lightwells, accessed via bridging plinths. Vertical load-bearing ashlar envelopes rectified to strict gravity alignment. Pitched rooflines with dormered mansards, prominent masonry chimney stacks with terracotta pots, and regular fenestration grids of 6-over-6 and 12-over-12 timber sash-and-case windows.
